title.narrative: Gender Equality and Empowerment of Women

description.narrative: The goal of the Project is to reduce poverty in rural Nepal by empowering poor rural women and members of other disadvantaged groups, such as ethnic and low-caste women. The objective is to improve the socioeconomic conditions of poor rural women through a process of economic, social, legal, and political empowerment by (i) strengthening their individual capabilities to improve their access to and control over assets; (ii) building group support for individual and collective action to influence and hold institutions accountable; and (iii) reforming Government institutions and processes to become gender-responsive and include previously marginalized women into development opportunities. The project components comprise (i) economic empowerment, (ii) legal empowerment, (iii) social empowerment, and (iv) institutional strengthening and project management. The components are mutually supporting to promote a virtuous circle of socioeconomic improvement among poor rural women.

Output: 1. Economic empowerment Increased income, assets, and employment opportunities for beneficiaries Indicator: 50% of those trained in microenterprise (ME) development have, at the end of the project, sustainable incremental income Progress/Status: 12,187 trained in business promotion and skill development trainings. Of the total, 6,300 have utilized into their business. Type of ME varied across districts, while goat keeping and vegetable farming were most common. These businesses helped to increase their income by 81% in average compared to base line. Poor rural women, including low caste and ethnic groups, empowered economically, socially, and politically.

50,000 women have improved and regular sources of production and income Progress/Status: Number of women who accessed to skills training, saving credit services and seed money support has exceeded the target. The average annual income of beneficiaries has increased about 81% compared to base line. Data Source: Same as above Actual value:

A total of 100,000 households have positive economic and social development impacts from the project Progress/Status: 51,445 women (at least 1 woman from 1 HH) became members in project initiated 9,392 groups; 31,416 women are involved in 800 ward level committees and also 31,841 women became members in 82 SCCs/Federation of whom 66,208 have received one or more types of training. 101,376 people have been benefited from project financed 3,548 community infrastructures. 88% of the beneficiaries have reported that project has brought positive change on their livelihoods. The increase in income is about 79.8%, 23.2% and 100.7% of dalit, indigenous people and other category of HH respectively. Data Source: -Project baseline survey measuring and monitoring evolving socio-economic conditions by gender, ethnicity and caste - Project surveys and monitoring and review - DDC and VDC records and comparison with periodic plans and targets - Project performance audit report and review Actual value:
